dana: Heads-up — onboarding Tempest-14B into staging. Need a quick sanity check on weights location + tokenizer quirks before I open a canary. I put weights at s3://redwood-tempest/weights/tempest14b/v1/ and tokenizer at s3://redwood-tempest/tokenizers/tempest14b/.

But serving config validation failed with a kv/caching error and the tokenizer is producing OOVs for leading-space tokens. Also noticed continuous batching seems to exceed `max_tokens_per_request` when prefix caching is on. Anyone available to quick-check?

kai: On it. Can you paste the exact validation error?

dana: Sure — paste from logs:
```
ERROR validate_config: kv_cache_shard_count mismatch between model and runtime (model=8, runtime=4)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "runtime/serve/validator.py", line 211, in validate
    raise ConfigValidationError(msg)
ConfigValidationError: kv cache config mismatch
```

Also from the runtime trace when a request with prefix cache hits:
```
WARN batcher: effective_token_count (prefix+request) 2048 > max_tokens_per_request 1024
```

sylvia: kv cache mismatch is usually the weights/manifest mismatch — did you split weights for 8 shards but leave runtime shards at 4? Did you re-run `tools/generate_manifest.py` after splitting?

Try: `python tools/generate_manifest.py --weights s3://redwood-tempest/weights/tempest14b/v1/ --out s3://redwood-tempest/manifests/tempest14b-v1.json`

Also tokenizer note: Tempest uses a legacy BPE variant that requires prefix-space normalization. Set `tokenizer.add_prefix_space = true` in tokenizer config (or you'll see OOVs for tokens that typically start with a space).

marc: For the batching behavior — remember the batcher counts cached prefix tokens toward `max_tokens_per_request`. Two quick tuning knobs that help: bump `max_tokens_per_request` to account for typical prefix sizes, and raise `max_tokens_per_batch` so the scheduler doesn't shed load prematurely. Example snippet we use for similar models:
```
batch_policy:
  max_tokens_per_request: 1536
  max_tokens_per_batch: 65536
  scheduler: continuous
  schedule_heuristic: latency_weighted
```

If you prefer fairness across users, `scheduler: fair` instead of `continuous`, but fair increases latency tail. Continuous gives higher throughput but you need smaller `cache_ttl_seconds` if your prefixes change often.

kai: Also check `tokenizer.eos_token_id` — manifest sometimes defaults to 0 but weights expect 2, which causes early truncation. Add explicit mapping in the manifest `vocab_map` or set `model_config.tokenizer.eos_token_id: 2`.

deploy-bot: deploy started for tempest14b-manifest v1 -> staging at 1967894350 :package:

dana: OK — action plan: 1) re-generate manifest with correct shard count, 2) update tokenizer config add_prefix_space=true and explicit eos_token_id, 3) bump batching values to max_request=1536 / max_batch=65536, 4) set cache_ttl_seconds=30 for staging and use `scheduler: continuous` for perf testing. Will run smoke and report back. Thanks y'all :rocket:

sylvia: LGTM. If you hit any weird tokenization diffs, ping me and I'll run a small compare script (diff_tokenized.py) across 2k sample prompts. :thumbsup:

kai: ping when logs show green or if the kv shard error persists.

marc: noted — if you want I can flip shard count on the runtime nodes to 8 temporarily to validate without re-splitting weights.

dana: I'll try manifest + tokenizer first. If still failing I'll ask you to flip the runtime shards. Thanks!
